driver: IEA WEI 2025 estimate of 2025 upstream oil and gas investment (just under USD 570 bn, 2024 prices) versus WEI 2026 outcome (USD 542 bn, 2025 prices)
note: Outcome over outlook = 0.951. Used for the optimism haircut (MODEL_HAIRCUT_AERO, MODEL_HAIRCUT_OFFICIAL), not as a growth shift. One point, one year ahead. The two figures are on DIFFERENT price bases (2024 against 2025 USD) and no deflator is in the repository, so the ratio mixes price and volume (TODO(data): rebase). It is an investment series, not aerospace, so it is not used for the aerospace haircut.

driver: Boeing 737 production rate reached in Q4 2025 (42 a month) versus the plan rate for 2026 (47 a month)
note: Outcome over outlook = 0.894. Used for the optimism haircut (MODEL_HAIRCUT_AERO, MODEL_HAIRCUT_OFFICIAL), not as a growth shift. This compares a rate reached in Q4 2025 with the rate planned for the following year, so it is the gap to be closed, not a final miss. Boeing's chief executive said it will take until 2027 to be stable at 47 a month (wing supply is the bottleneck), which confirms a slip of about one year.

driver: Airbus 2026 deliveries: guidance of about 870 versus the full year implied by nine months (547) at the 2025 seasonality (507 of 793 delivered in the first nine months)
note: Outcome over outlook = 0.983. Used for the optimism haircut (MODEL_HAIRCUT_AERO, MODEL_HAIRCUT_OFFICIAL), not as a growth shift. A projection of the outcome, not a final outcome. Reaching 870 needs about 323 deliveries in Q4 against 286 in Q4 2025. Pratt and Whitney engine shortages are the stated drag.

driver: CFM LEAP deliveries 2026: GE guidance of high teens growth (18 percent) versus GE nine month growth of 26 percent
note: Outcome over outlook = 1.068. Used for the optimism haircut (MODEL_HAIRCUT_AERO, MODEL_HAIRCUT_OFFICIAL), not as a growth shift. Engines beat guidance while airframe rates slipped: counter evidence, a ratio above 1. The nine month growth overstates the full year, because Q3 grew only 4.7 percent (535 against 511). Nine months plus a flat to plus 5 percent Q4 on the 562 engines of Q4 2025 gives full year growth of 18 to 20 percent, a ratio of 1.000 to 1.014.

driver: Aircraft deliveries or fleet history
note: TODO(data): only two LEAP delivery points are logged (1,407 in 2024, 1,802 in 2025). Aircraft fleet history is shown in Airbus charts but not as a table. The haircut uses the Boeing 737 rate plan, the Airbus 2026 run rate, the LEAP guidance and (for non aerospace industries) the IEA WEI vintage as the available plan against outcome points.
